incident.name: McGraw-Hill Salesforce Misconfiguration
incident.description: ShinyHunters exploited a misconfigured Salesforce Experience Cloud guest user permission granting unauthenticated access to the /s/sfsites/aura endpoint. No exploit needed — just a misconfigured SaaS. 13.5M records confirmed by HIBP. DIVD issued advisory DIVD-2026-00005 confirming industry-wide issue.
incident.root_cause: Salesforce guest user over-permissioning, no continuous SaaS configuration monitoring
incident.lessons: SaaS configuration drift is a critical attack surface. Continuous posture management is required — annual audits are insufficient.

relatedIncidents.name: PowerSchool Data Breach
relatedIncidents.description: Attackers used stolen credentials to access PowerSchool's student information system, exposing data of 62M+ students and teachers across thousands of school districts in the US and Canada.
relatedIncidents.root_cause: No MFA on maintenance portal, credentials stolen via infostealer malware
relatedIncidents.lessons: Education sector SIS platforms hold sensitive PII for millions of minors and require MFA and strict access controls.

relatedIncidents.name: Aura Identity Protection Breach
relatedIncidents.description: Attacker used AI voice cloning to impersonate a trusted contact and social-engineer an Aura employee into granting system access. 900,000 records accessed in ~1 hour. Ironic: Aura sells identity theft protection services.
relatedIncidents.root_cause: AI-assisted vishing, no out-of-band verification for access requests
relatedIncidents.lessons: AI voice cloning makes vishing indistinguishable from real calls. All access requests via phone must be verified through a separate channel.

relatedIncidents.name: ADT Vishing + Salesforce Breach
relatedIncidents.description: ShinyHunters used vishing to compromise one employee's Okta SSO account, gaining full Salesforce access. 5.5M records confirmed by HIBP including names, addresses, partial SSNs. ADT's third breach in two years.
relatedIncidents.root_cause: No phishing-resistant MFA on SSO, no anomaly detection for bulk CRM exports
relatedIncidents.lessons: SSO without FIDO2 MFA is a single point of failure. Bulk CRM data exports must trigger alerts regardless of authentication method.
